recipe.title: Greek Pastitsio Bake with Tomato-Onion Salad
recipe.description: Cinnamon-scented lean beef and tomato under whole wheat pasta, topped with a thin ultra-filtered milk custard that browns in blistered patches. The butter béchamel is gone — a milk-and-egg custard with a dusting of parmesan does the same job. Alongside: a sharp red wine vinegar tomato and onion salad.

ingredients.item: Whole wheat penne or ziti (new buy)
Extra virgin olive oil for salad (new buy)

steps.title: Heat oven, start pasta water
steps.content: Set the oven to 200C/400F. Put a pot of salted water on high heat for the pasta.

steps.title: Brown the beef
steps.content: Chop the white onion fine. Heat 12 g olive oil in a skillet over medium-high (7/10). Add beef, break it up and let it sit undisturbed 3 minutes for a real brown crust, then stir and cook 3 more. Drain off any rendered fat. Add onion and garlic, cook 3 minutes.

steps.title: Cinnamon tomato sauce
steps.content: Stir in cinnamon, Italian seasoning and tomato paste; cook 1 minute to toast. Add the 300 g tomatoes, chopped, plus a splash of water. Drop to a simmer (3-4/10) and cook 10 minutes until thick and glossy. Salt and pepper to taste.

steps.title: Cook the pasta
steps.content: While the sauce simmers, boil the pasta 2 minutes shy of package time. Drain and toss with the remaining 8 g olive oil so it doesn't clump.

steps.title: Custard top
steps.content: Whisk the milk, egg, 10 g of the parmesan, salt and pepper in a bowl until smooth. Pro tip: keep it thin — it should pour like cream, not batter.

steps.title: Layer and bake
steps.content: Spread the meat sauce in a small baking dish (about 20x20 cm). Layer the pasta over it evenly, pour the custard over so it seeps between the pasta, and dust with the remaining 10 g parmesan. Bake 25 minutes at 200C/400F, until set and browned in blistered patches. If it's pale, broil 2 minutes.

steps.title: Make the salad
steps.content: With 10 minutes left on the bake: slice the 250 g tomatoes into wedges and the red onion paper-thin. Toss with the red wine vinegar, 8 g olive oil, chopped parsley, salt and pepper. Let it sit — the onion softens and the tomatoes give up juice for the dressing.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.content: Let the bake rest 8 minutes off the heat so it slices cleanly. Cut in squares, spoon the salad and its juices alongside.

recipe.notes: Per serving: ~38 g protein, ~615 cal, ~4.5 g saturated fat, 0 g added sugar, ~10 g fiber. New buys: 93% ground beef, whole wheat penne, tomato paste, ultra-filtered milk, parmesan, extra virgin olive oil, ground cinnamon, red onion, fresh parsley. Leftovers keep 3 days; reheat on Steam in the Tovala so the custard stays soft, then 1 minute Broil to re-crisp the top. Pro tip: the undisturbed 3 minutes on the beef is where the flavor is — don't stir early. Liver note: the classic butter-and-flour béchamel (easily 15 g saturated fat a serving) is replaced by a thin ultra-filtered milk and egg custard, the pasta is whole wheat, and lean 93% beef is drained — same dish, a fraction of the saturated fat.

recipe.title: Greek Baked Beef & Zucchini Pastitsio-Style
recipe.description: Soft whole wheat pasta under a cinnamon-scented tomato-beef and zucchini layer, topped with a light milk-and-egg custard that browns golden. All the comfort of pastitsio with the butter béchamel swapped for a milk custard. Served with a sharp tomato-onion salad.

steps.title: Heat the oven and boil water
steps.content: Heat the oven to 200C/400F. Put a pot of salted water on high heat for the pasta.

steps.title: Cook the pasta short
steps.content: Boil the 80 g whole wheat pasta 2 minutes less than the package says — it finishes in the oven. Drain and toss with 5 g of the olive oil so it doesn't clump.

steps.title: Brown the beef
steps.content: Meanwhile, heat 10 g olive oil in a large skillet over medium-high (7/10). Add the diced onion and cook 3 minutes, then the beef. Break it up and let it brown properly, 5-6 minutes — don't stir constantly, you want colour. Drain off any fat. Pro tip: the browning is the flavour here, there's no butter to hide behind.

steps.title: Build the tomato layer
steps.content: Stir in the garlic, cinnamon, 1 tsp oregano, tomato paste, chopped tomatoes and the diced zucchini. Season with salt and pepper. Simmer at 3-4/10 for 10 minutes until thick and just barely saucy, not wet.

steps.title: Custard top
steps.content: Whisk the milk, egg, parmesan, a pinch of salt and plenty of pepper in a bowl until smooth.

steps.title: Assemble and bake
steps.content: Spread the pasta in a small baking dish (about 20x20 cm), spoon the beef mixture over it evenly, then pour the milk-egg mixture over the top. Bake at 200C/400F for 25-30 minutes, until set and golden-spotted on top. If it's pale at the end, broil 2 minutes.

steps.title: Make the salad while it bakes
steps.content: Cut the salad tomatoes into wedges and slice the 50 g onion thin. Toss with the red wine vinegar, the last 5 g olive oil, 1/2 tsp oregano, salt and pepper. Let it sit until dinner — the onion softens and the tomatoes give up juice for the dressing.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.content: Let the bake rest 8-10 minutes out of the oven so the custard firms and cuts cleanly. Cut in two, serve with the salad alongside.

recipe.notes: Per serving: ~38 g protein, ~570 cal, ~5.5 g saturated fat, 0 g added sugar, ~9 g fiber. New buys: 93% ground beef, whole wheat pasta, zucchini, tomato paste, ground cinnamon, dried oregano, olive oil, reduced fat milk, parmesan. Leftovers keep 3 days; reheat on Tovala Steam so the custard doesn't dry out. Pro tips: undercook the pasta, drain the beef fat, and rest before cutting. Liver note: the classic butter-and-flour béchamel is replaced by a milk-and-egg custard and the pasta is whole wheat, which drops the saturated fat by more than half and adds the fiber.
